article: XSS and CSRF: attack models and layered defenses
findings: Reframed the exploit-kit statement so XSS redirection is not presented as sufficient by itself to infect a computer; the example now notes that malware delivery also depends on exploitable browser vulnerabilities.

Clarified that the CSP host-allowlist snippet is simplified and that CSP is an additional layer, not a replacement for context-aware encoding, safe DOM APIs, or HTML sanitization; recommends nonce/hash-based strict policies where practical.
Made the CSRF scenario explicitly assume browser/profile permission to send cross-site third-party cookies, in addition to SameSite=None; Secure and missing server-side checks.
Added shared OWASP DOM-XSS and CSP guidance and MDN CSRF/Set-Cookie references in all thirteen editions; preserved the existing OWASP XSS and CSRF citations.
Compared the complete Japanese article with all twelve translations; preserved original publication dates and updated lastmod.

meaning.note: Compared the complete edition with Japanese: stored/reflected/DOM-based XSS and their overlap; attacker-controlled sources and dangerous sinks; impact limits; contextual output encoding, framework escape hatches, CSP, HttpOnly; the CSRF threat model; synchronizer token, signed double-submit, Origin and SameSite controls; same-site versus same-origin; and the XSS/CSRF relationship.

terminology.note: Checked localized terminology for XSS/CSRF, DOM source/sink, same-origin policy, site/origin boundaries, output encoding/escaping, sanitization, CSP, nonce/hash, HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookies, CSRF token, Origin, and HMAC-signed double-submit.

mathematics.note: This article contains no mathematical claims or formulas requiring a mathematics review.

code.note: Reviewed the CSP header example and the localized Mermaid attack-flow diagram for structure and meaning. The explanatory cross-site form example was compared as text. No browser exploit, application endpoint, or policy was executed; no Mermaid rendering integration test was run.

links.note: Checked six shared primary references across all editions: OWASP XSS prevention, CSRF prevention, DOM-based XSS, CSP, and MDN CSRF and Set-Cookie documentation. Added the four missing OWASP/MDN references in every translation. Reachability beyond the cited web lookup and per-browser behavior are not certified.
